mcqs.question: Which of the following changes will increase the magnetic field strength of an electromagnet the most?

options.A: Doubling the number of turns while keeping the current the same
options.B: Doubling the current while keeping the number of turns the same
options.C: Using a core material with lower magnetic permeability
options.D: Increasing the length of the coil

mcqs.answer: Doubling the current while keeping the number of turns the same
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field inside a solenoid (and hence an electromagnet) is given by B = μ₀μ_r (N/L) I, where N is the total number of turns, L is the length of the coil and I is the current. Doubling the current directly doubles B, whereas changing the core to a material with lower permeability would actually reduce the field. Increasing the length reduces the turn density (N/L) and therefore weakens the field. Hence, doubling the current yields the greatest increase in strength.

mcqs.question: Which of the following devices relies on an electromagnet to operate?

options.B: Bar magnet used in a compass

mcqs.explanation: An electric bell contains a coil that becomes magnetised when current flows, attracting a ferromagnetic armature to produce the ringing sound. The other options either use permanent magnets or are unrelated to electromagnetism, so the electric bell is the correct example of a practical application of an electromagnet.

mcqs.question: A solenoid is best described as:

options.A: A tightly wound coil of wire that produces a uniform magnetic field inside when electric current passes through it
options.B: A straight piece of wire that carries current without generating any magnetic field
options.C: A pair of permanent magnets placed side by side
options.D: A hollow tube filled with liquid metal

mcqs.answer: A tightly wound coil of wire that produces a uniform magnetic field inside when electric current passes through it
mcqs.explanation: When a current flows through many turns of wire arranged in a cylindrical shape, the magnetic field lines inside become nearly parallel and uniform, which is the defining characteristic of a solenoid. The other options do not describe this arrangement or its magnetic effect.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand magnetic field of a solenoid
mcqs.question: What is the direction of the magnetic field inside a solenoid when the current flows clockwise as seen from one end?

options.A: From south to north outside the solenoid
options.B: Along the axis from that end toward the opposite end, following the right‑hand grip rule
options.D: Perpendicular to the plane of the coil

mcqs.answer: Along the axis from that end toward the opposite end, following the right‑hand grip rule
mcqs.explanation: Using the right‑hand grip rule, if the fingers follow the direction of current (clockwise when viewed from the end), the thumb points in the direction of the magnetic field inside the solenoid. Hence the field runs along the axis from that end toward the other. The other options misrepresent the field direction.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an electromagnet from a permanent magnet?

options.A: An electromagnet requires electric current to produce a magnetic field, whereas a permanent magnet produces a field without any current
options.B: An electromagnet is always stronger than any permanent magnet, regardless of size
options.C: A permanent magnet can be turned on and off by a switch, while an electromagnet cannot
options.D: Both electromagnets and permanent magnets need a continuous supply of electricity to retain their magnetism

mcqs.answer: An electromagnet requires electric current to produce a magnetic field, whereas a permanent magnet produces a field without any current
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of an electromagnet is that its magnetic field exists only while current flows through its coil. A permanent magnet retains its magnetism without any external power. The other statements are inaccurate regarding strength, controllability, and power requirements.

mcqs.question: Which modification will NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet?

options.A: Increasing the current flowing through the coil
options.B: Increasing the number of turns in the coil
options.C: Inserting a soft iron core inside the coil
options.D: Increasing the radius of the coil while keeping the number of turns constant

mcqs.answer: Increasing the radius of the coil while keeping the number of turns constant
mcqs.explanation: Strength depends on turn density (turns per unit length) and current. Increasing radius spreads the turns over a larger area, reducing turn density and thus weakening the field. The other three actions (more current, more turns, iron core) all enhance the magnetic field.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a common industrial use of an electromagnet?

options.C: Scrapyard crane that lifts heavy metal objects

mcqs.answer: Scrapyard crane that lifts heavy metal objects
mcqs.explanation: Scrapyard cranes employ powerful electromagnets to pick up and release heavy ferrous pieces. MRI machines use superconducting magnets, electric motors use rotating magnetic fields, and speakers use a permanent magnet with a coil, so the crane is the direct example of an electromagnet application.

mcqs.question: A student wraps insulated copper wire tightly around a clean iron nail, connects the ends to a battery, and the nail becomes magnetised. Which device has the student essentially created?
mcqs.explanation: The wound coil around the iron nail forms a solenoid. When current passes, the iron core becomes magnetised, turning the assembly into an electromagnet. It is not a permanent magnet because the magnetism disappears when the current is switched off, nor is it a capacitor or resistor.
